meta.title: Riptide: free, open-source download manager for Windows
meta.description: A free, open-source download manager for Windows. Parallel connections, exact resume, SHA-256 verified. No ads, no telemetry, no accounts. English and Arabic.
meta.ogAlt: Riptide: download faster, every byte verified

hero.lead: A free, open-source download manager. Parallel connections, exact resume, SHA‑256 checks.

sim.label: Simulation of a download in progress. An illustration, not a measurement.

streams.lead: Riptide pulls a file down several lanes at once, then rebuilds it byte for byte.
streams.label: The Riptide logo is drawn by three streams, which then run down parallel lanes into one file.

app.lead: Dense, calm, keyboard-friendly. Light and dark, English and Arabic.
app.altLight: The Riptide downloads list in the light theme: segmented progress bars, speeds, time left and status for each file
app.altDark: The Riptide downloads list in the dark theme: segmented progress bars, speeds, time left and status for each file
app.winLabel: The Riptide desktop app, with four numbered annotations.

callouts.t: Checksum mismatches are caught, not hidden

speed.lead: A connection that finishes early takes over half of a slower one's range. Nothing sits idle.
speed.note: A simulation, not a benchmark. Real speed depends on your connection and the server.
speed.label: Simulation: eight connections fill one file. A connection that finishes early takes over half of a slower one's range.

integrity.lead: Progress is saved every second. Only a matching checksum makes a download Completed.

resume.p: Riptide continues at the saved byte. If the file changed on the server, it starts over.
resume.label: Simulation: a power cut stops a download, and it resumes from the same byte.

verify.p: The .rtpart file is hashed and compared. Only a match becomes the final file.
verify.label: The partial file is checked with SHA-256, then renamed into place.

details.p: Segment map, speed graph and a limit per download.
details.alt: The details drawer: 8 of 8 connections, a per-segment progress map, a speed graph for the last minute and the source link

junk.p: Free and open source. Nothing phones home.

add.p: Paste a link. Size, resume support and connections are verified first.
add.alt: The Add download dialog: the link is already checked (3.36 GB, resumable, multiple connections), with file name, category, folder and a connections picker

langs.p: Fully mirrored right to left. Switch live.
langs.altAr: The same list in Arabic, mirrored right to left

video.p: Paste a page link and Riptide fetches the video.

peruser.p: Per-user install, plus a portable zip.

vs.title: Versus paid managers.
vs.lead: Plain facts about Riptide next to what is generally true of paid products.
vs.footnote: We name no product. Check any vendor's own documentation before you decide.

oss.title: Built in the open.
oss.lead: App: GPL-3.0. Engine: MIT or Apache-2.0. Every line is on GitHub.

feedback.title: Found a rough edge?
feedback.lead: It's an alpha. Your reports decide what gets fixed first.

items.a: Yes. No paid tier, no license key, no trial. The code is open source.

items.q: How do I know my download is genuine?
items.a: Every release lists SHA-256 checksums. Run certutil -hashfile with the file name and SHA256, then compare the result with the list.

items.q: Does it work with my browser?
items.a: Yes: Chrome, Edge and Firefox, through the extension. Store listings are on the way; until then, load it from GitHub.
Video pages work through bundled yt-dlp in the main branch and ship in the next release.
Windows 10 and 11 for now. The engine is portable, but there is no date for other platforms.

meta.title: Privacy policy · Riptide
meta.description: Riptide and its browser extension collect nothing: no telemetry, no accounts, no analytics. What stays on your computer and the few network requests Riptide makes.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.updated: Last updated: 19 October 2026. Applies to the Riptide desktop app, the Riptide CLI, the Riptide browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox, and this website.
privacy.lede: Short version: Riptide collects nothing. There is no telemetry, no analytics, no account and no advertising. Your downloads, settings and history stay on your computer, and nobody, including the people who make Riptide, receives any of it.

paras: Nothing. Riptide has no server of its own. The app, the CLI and the extension do not send usage statistics, crash reports, identifiers or any other information to us or to anyone else.
Riptide does not use accounts, so there is no sign-up, no e-mail address and no profile.

The download list, its progress and your settings are kept in a local database in your user profile (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Riptide on Windows). Log files are written to the same folder; the addresses in them have their query strings removed and cookies, passwords and authorization headers are never written to them.
You can delete any of this at any time by removing downloads from the list or by deleting the folder.
Riptide connects to the servers of the files you choose to download, and to nothing else on your behalf.

The only request it makes on its own is an optional check for a new version against GitHub Releases (github.com). It sends nothing about you beyond what any web request carries, such as your IP address, and it can be turned off in Settings. GitHub's own privacy statement applies to that request.

The extension's only job is to hand downloads from your browser to the Riptide app on the same computer. It talks to the app through the browser's Native Messaging channel; it has no network access of its own, loads no remote code and contains no analytics.

When it hands over a download it passes the download address, the suggested file name, the referring page and the browser's user agent to the local app. Your rules and language choice are saved in the browser's extension storage and never leave the browser.

Some downloads only work when you are signed in. For those, the extension reads the browser's cookies for the address being downloaded, and only that address, and passes them to the local Riptide app.

Riptide sends those cookies only to the same site they belong to, for that one download, and never to another site, including after a redirect to a different origin. They are kept in a separate local table while the download is in progress, are never written to logs, and are deleted as soon as the download completes or is removed.

This site is a set of static pages hosted on GitHub Pages. It uses no cookies, no analytics and no trackers, and it loads nothing from third parties: fonts, images and scripts come from the same origin. The only thing it stores is your light or dark theme choice, in your own browser. GitHub may keep ordinary server logs under its own privacy policy.
The Feedback section links to GitHub issue forms. What you write there is public on GitHub and governed by GitHub's terms and privacy statement; this site never sees it.

Because we receive no data, we have nothing to share, sell or transfer, and nothing is used for advertising, credit decisions or any purpose other than your downloads. Riptide is not directed at children and collects no information from anyone.

If this policy changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new date, and the history of the page is public in the source repository. Questions are welcome as an issue on GitHub at github.com/LayanJarrar1/Riptide/issues.
